name: Ofir
title: Descendant of Joktan's lineage
summary: Ofir was a son of Joktan, who was a descendant of Shem, Noah's son. He is best known as the origin of the name for a legendary land rich in gold called Ophir, which became famous during Solomon's time for its wealth. The name Ophir appears in the Bible's genealogies and is associated with an area known for gold, precious stones, and other treasures.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy after Noah
keyEvents.description: Ofir is listed as one of Joktans thirteen sons in the post-flood genealogy, as part of Sems lineage.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in the Chronicles genealogy
keyEvents.description: Ofir is mentioned again in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles as one of Joktans sons, confirming his place in Sems line.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's gold shipments from the land of Ofir
keyEvents.description: The land of Ofir, named after the person Ofir, was known as a source of large amounts of gold that King Solomon received through his fleet.

keyEvents.title: Ofir gold as a symbol of wealth
keyEvents.description: Ofir gold was used as an image of great value and wealth in the book of Job and by the prophet Isaiah.

keyEvents.title: Ophir Gold in the Book of Psalms
keyEvents.description: In Psalm 45, a royal wedding psalm, gold from Ophir is mentioned as an adornment for the queen, showing the name Ophir's connection to what is most precious.
